MD1 directory precedence
syNOPSIS order in the same snapshot, modprobe.d.5.scd lines 9-17:
@SYSCONFDIR@/modprobe.d/*.conf, /run/modprobe.d/*.conf, /usr/local/lib/modprobe.d/*.conf,
@DISTCONFDIR@/modprobe.d/*.conf, /lib/modprobe.d/*.conf
mechanism, libkmod-config.c:1025 iterates config_paths in that order and calls conf_files_list
(line 1007 passes every accepted directory entry to conf_files_insert_sorted).
Default list (supplementary fetch, libkmod/libkmod.c:44-52 @v34): SYSCONFDIR/modprobe.d,
/run/modprobe.d, /usr/local/lib/modprobe.d, DISTCONFDIR/modprobe.d, /lib/modprobe.d, NULL
— identical order to SYNOPSIS, so quote (a) is a description of code, not just of docs.
MD2 lexicographic order + partial replacement
libkmod-config.c:937 `if ((cmp = strcmp(name, cf->name)) <= 0) break;` — the sort key is the
FILE NAME only; the directory is not part of the key. One global name-sorted list is then walked
at 1058-1081, so parse order is lexicographic across all directories, as quote (b) states.
Quote b2 states the replace/partial-replace consequence but is 35 words: unusable as a quote cell.
MD3 duplicate rejection at insertion
libkmod-config.c:920 conf_files_insert_sorted(); 941-944 `if (cmp == 0) ... return -EEXIST`.
Because directories are visited in precedence order, the FIRST copy of a name is inserted and every
later copy of that name is dropped with -EEXIST — MD1 and MD3 are the same branch, seen from two sides.
MD4 kcmdline parsed after the files
libkmod-config.c:1083 kmod_config_parse_kcmdline(config); sits after the 1058-1081 file loop and
before `return 0;` at 1085 — into the same `config` object. Merge is by append, not replacement:
kmod_config_add_options (155-181) appends every options entry, and kmod_module_get_options
(supplementary fetch libkmod-module.c:1116-1155 @v34) concatenates all matching entries in list
order, so the kcmdline options are appended after the file-derived ones. MD4's wording must stay
"land in the same config object" and must NOT claim a replacement/override.
MD5 dry-run
modprobe.c:128 usage text is the only CLI-level statement; flag propagation at 623-624
(`if (dry_run) flags |= KMOD_PROBE_DRY_RUN;`). Neither line contains a pipe or a double quote.
(Two other `if (dry_run)` sites exist at 298 and 323 in the command/insert paths.)
MD6 blacklist alias-only by default
modprobe.c:626 sets KMOD_PROBE_APPLY_BLACKLIST_ALIAS_ONLY unconditionally; 628-629 adds
KMOD_PROBE_APPLY_BLACKLIST only when use_blacklist (-b/--use-blacklist). Behaviour, supplementary
fetch libkmod/libkmod-module.c:1023-1031 @v34: if the module is blacklisted and it has an alias and
ALIAS_ONLY is set, the probe stops; a directly named (non-alias) module is stopped only when
APPLY_BLACKLIST or APPLY_BLACKLIST_ALL is set. So MD6 as drafted is accurate for modprobe(8).
